solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: 'Mass plus one' shown by American mathematician

parts.note: a mass of people is a mob
surface padding: joins the next piece on
surface padding: joins the next piece on

explanation.surface: A quotation attributed to an American mathematician, as if 'mass plus one' were a famous formula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like physics shorthand for M, but it is a whole word here: a crowd, a MOB.
explanation.definitionFit: August Möbius was the German mathematician of the one-sided Möbius strip.

clue.text: 1000 different clues in force

indicators.note: the letters of CLUES appear in a different order

explanation.surface: A thousand clues, all different, that are currently in force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like part of the picture; it is the definition, and 'in' simply joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle is power or force, as in 'political muscle'.

clue.text: Sweetener to get improper rebates about rugs essentially

indicators.note: the shuffled REBATES go about, around, the middle of rugs
improper rebates are ones not in the proper order

parts.note: the middle two letters of rUGs

explanation.surface: A bribe, a 'sweetener', paid through dodgy rebates on a rug deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetener' suggests a bribe, which suits the improper rebates, but it is the literal sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: this sugar, refined from sugar beet, is one kind of sweetener.

clue.text: Dishevelled drunk emptied container

indicators.note: the words 'drunk emptied' act as a container holding the answer

explanation.surface: A dishevelled drunk has emptied a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emptied' tempts you to take the outer letters of 'drunk', but 'container' tells you the answer is held within the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: literally 'uncombed', so with hair in a mess.

clue.text: Plans revolutionary carpet in South Africa

indicators.note: the revolutionary's carpet sits in the country, between its S and A

explanation.surface: Plans for a revolutionary carpet made in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a reversal signal; it is CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Schemata is the plural of schema, a plan or outline.

clue.text: Floating naiad corpse richly arrayed

indicators.note: letters that are floating drift into a new order

explanation.surface: A drowned water nymph floats in fine clothes, like Ophelia.
explanation.walkthrough: A naiad is a water nymph, which is why her corpse is floating.
explanation.definitionFit: Caparisoned means decked out in rich trappings, originally of a horse.

clue.text: Despite all that's gone before, it's all square as things are

parts.note: surface padding: first word of the phrase 'all square'

explanation.surface: A sports commentator notes the score is level whatever happened earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All square' is sporting language for a level score.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Even now' means still, in spite of everything that has happened.

clue.text: Block part of ear

definitions.meaning: the iron block a smith hammers on
the incus bone of the middle ear

explanation.walkthrough: The anvil, or incus, is one of three tiny bones in the middle ear, named for its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An anvil is a smith's iron block, and also the incus, a small bone of the middle ear.

clue.text: Twice in the past you would support the whole 'married' nonsense

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece sits underneath

parts.note: the whole is all of it
YE is the old form of you, taken twice

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned grumble about the whole business of marriage being nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All my eye (and Betty Martin)' is dated British slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated British idiom, fuller form 'all my eye and Betty Martin', used to dismiss something as rubbish.

clue.text: Chief sound of rattle

indicators.note: we want the sound of a word, not its spelling

explanation.surface: The chief noise a rattle makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chief sound' reads as 'main noise', but 'Chief' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the title of an Arab tribal leader or head of a family.

clue.text: Have Paul busted for disturbance

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Paul gets arrested for causing a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busted' reads as arrested, which fits a disturbance; here it means broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: literally a heaving up of the ground, figuratively any violent upset.

clue.text: Unsuccessful business stupidly masks role

indicators.note: the letters are arranged stupidly, out of order

explanation.surface: A failing firm foolishly hides what it really does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masks' looks like a verb acting on 'role'; both are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss-maker is a business that loses money.

clue.text: Royal commode's broken — it's the end of the world!

indicators.note: a broken commode has its letters smashed apart

explanation.surface: The royal lavatory is broken, a palace catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: A commode is a chair hiding a chamber pot, which gives the surface its comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingdom come is the next world, as in 'until kingdom come': the end of the world.

clue.text: Life of royal mistress unknown

parts.note: Nell Gwyn, mistress of Charles II
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z

explanation.surface: The biography of a king's mistress whose name has been lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Life of' looks like a biography; 'Life' alone is the definition, through the British phrase 'not on your nelly', meaning 'not on your life'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelly is rhyming slang: Nelly Duff = puff = breath, life.

clue.text: Steam-roller's to secure a private road …

definitions.note: used as a verb: to steamroller

parts.note: to secure something is to get it
a private thing is one's own

explanation.surface: A steamroller's job is to lay a private road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steam-roller' looks like the machine, but it is the verb: to flatten opposition. The dots run on into 17 across.
explanation.definitionFit: To steamroller people is to force through what you want: to get one's own way.

clue.text: Your old master embraced by Oscar in shrub

parts.note: M for Master, as in MA

explanation.surface: An old master is caught in a bush with Oscar, a scandal for Wilde.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' tempts toward the phonetic-alphabet O; it is Oscar Wilde.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: this creeping aromatic herb is a low woody plant, so one kind of shrub.

clue.text: Take first shot at golf ball? No — change ends to hit cricket ball

indicators.note: change ends means the two halves of the golf shot swap ends

parts.note: to drive off is to tee off, taking the first stroke
surface padding: waves away the golf ball in favour of cricket

explanation.surface: A golfer abandons the tee shot and switches to cricket instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The off side in cricket is the side of the pitch the batter faces.
explanation.definitionFit: To off-drive is to hit the ball forward on the off side with a straight bat.

clue.text: … irrevocably, and avoid ruffling an old lady endlessly

parts.note: to forgo is to do without

explanation.surface: Continuing 14: once you've got your way, stop bothering an elderly woman for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An old lady' reads as one person; the words are separate fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for 'permanently', with no going back.

clue.text: Up in the air, cross, having taken time for female in public

parts.note: to overfly is to cross in the air

explanation.surface: Someone flares up in public, cross and up in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up in the air' and 'cross' look like two moods; together they describe overflying.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: done openly rather than covertly, for all to see.

clue.text: It inspires aged sailor to return with gold

parts.note: ae., short for Latin aetatis, 'aged', as on memorials

explanation.surface: An old seaman is encouraged to come home with treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspires' looks like encouragement; literally, to inspire is to breathe air in.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerator pumps air into something, so it in-spires in the literal sense.

clue.text: Take offence with headgear

definitions.meaning: to bristle with resentment, head tossed back

explanation.walkthrough: A bridle is the set of straps round a horse's head, so 'headgear' is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb is a horse tossing its head back against the reins, hence showing offence; the noun is the harness on a horse's head.

clue.text: Diamonds scrape flat stone

explanation.surface: Scraping diamonds out of flat stone.
explanation.walkthrough: In the game 'ducks and drakes' flat stones are skimmed across water; each is a drake.
explanation.definitionFit: A drake is a flat stone skimmed across water.

clue.text: Hold hard bit of sugar found in a barrel

indicators.note: just one bit, the first letter, of sugar

explanation.surface: Keep hold of the sugar lump found in a barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold hard' reads as grip; it is an old command to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Avast is the sailor's cry to stop, and 'hold hard!' likewise means stop.

clue.text: One examines failing trade in area in recession

indicators.note: a failing trade is going wrong, its letters out of order

explanation.surface: An economist studies a trade failing across a region in recession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recession' fits the economic surface, but here it means moving backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A moderator checks examiners' marking, so is one who examines.

clue.text: While fighting — or not

definitions.meaning: split as two words, engaged in battle

explanation.walkthrough: Split one way the letters give IN ACTION, fighting; read whole they give INACTION, not doing anything.
explanation.definitionFit: In action means in combat; inaction means doing nothing.

clue.text: Remained supported

definitions.meaning: past tense of stay, prop up

explanation.walkthrough: A mast is stayed when ropes called stays support it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stayed is the past of stay, remain, and also of stay, to prop up, as in a mast stayed with ropes.

clue.text: Admission with no charge? That's not right

definitions.text: Admission with no charge? That's not right

parts.note: admission with no charge is free entry

explanation.surface: A visitor complains that free admission turned out to cost money.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R from ENTRY FREE and you get what makes free entry wrong: a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry fee is exactly what denies admission with no charge.

clue.text: Band releases broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast words are heard, not seen

explanation.surface: A music group puts out new releases on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' and 'releases' paint a pop group; a band here is a decorative strip.
explanation.definitionFit: A frieze is a horizontal decorative band along a wall.
